description: A home battery's plan from the half hour under way to the end of tomorrow, on the tariff's real prices (Agile's, and Agile Outgoing's, estimated beyond what Octopus has published), half hour by half hour: charge from the grid, hold, run the house (self-use), export, or send the sun to the grid – the cheapest way through, counting the battery's losses and wear. Exporting follows what the export tariff pays for – everything on Octopus's, only what the panels put in on the others – unless `battery_export=all` says the home is paid for what the battery charged from the grid too. A battery without panels gives `export` (Octopus's `outgoing`, `agile-outgoing` or `prime-outgoing`, `eon-next-export-premium` for a battery E.ON fitted, or `fixed` with `export_rate`) and trades on the grid: charging cheap, exporting at the peak. Smart Export Guarantee tariffs pay only for what panels made, so not a battery on its own. `now` is what to set this half hour; `settings` the few changes worth typing into the inverter's app. For a typical home of `usage`; give `soc` (the battery's charge now) for a plan from where it is. Advice and data for the owner's own automation – Renewably never controls a battery.

battery_export.description: What the battery may export: `terms` (default) what the export terms pay for – on Octopus's export tariffs everything, on the others only what the panels put in; without panels everything, once `export` is given; `all` what it charged from the grid too, on any export tariff – check the supplier pays for that; `solar` only what the panels put in, even on Octopus's; `never`.

ceiling.description: Never charged above this, per cent (10-100, default 100; above `reserve`) – for an inverter set to stop short of full.

export.description: How export is paid: `paired` (the tariff's own export tariff, default), `fixed` (with export_rate), `fit` (the Feed-in Tariff's deemed export: paid whatever is exported, so the sun used at home gives nothing up), `none`, or an export tariff's key from list_tariffs?direction=export (used where the tariff can have it, else its own).

export_limit.description: The home's export limit, kW (0-30, default 3.68: a G98 connection).

grid_charging.description: `1` (default) may charge from the grid; `0` only from the panels.

rate.description: Charge and discharge rate, kW (0.5-15, default 3).

region.description: Agile region: a letter A-P, the slug from list_regions (eg `C` or `london`), or one of the well-known places list_regions lists for it (eg `Manchester`).

reserve.description: Never below this, per cent (0-90, default 0).

soc.description: The battery's charge now, per cent (0-100). Default: at its reserve.

solar_facing.description: The way they face: S, SE, SW, E, W, NE, NW or N – or a bearing in degrees (south is 180). Default S.

solar_inverter_kw.description: The inverter's limit, kW (0.5-50), if smaller than the panels.

solar_kwp.description: The home's solar panels, kWp (0.2-50): the answer then counts their forecast spare sun – see the docs' Solar panels section.

solar_pitch.description: Their angle from flat, degrees (0-90, default 35).

tariff.description: A tariff's key from list_tariffs (default `agile`), eg `go`, `edf-go-electric`, `eon-next-drive`.

usage.description: The home's electricity use, kWh a year (500-30000, default 2500).

wear.description: The battery's wear for each kWh it gives back, pence (0-20, default 2).
